terms.gloss: challenge, call out (to a game, a race, a fight)
terms.grammar: verb, first conjugation: ad or in with the accusative of the contest
evidence: Plaut. Curc. 355: prōvocat mē in āleam
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “to call out, challenge, invite one to any thing (as to play, sing, drink, fight)”: ad pugnam (Cic. Tusc. 4.49), to a race (Plautus). Of rivals, to compete with (Quintilian, Pliny). “A challenge” is best given with the verb: prōvocātiō is classically an appeal to the people.

phrases.latin: postquam cēnātī atque appōtī, tālōs poscit sibi in manum, prōvocat mē in āleam, ut ego lūdam
phrases.english: after dinner and drinks he calls for the dice and challenges me to a game

phrases.latin: circumferēns inde trucēs mināciter oculōs ad procerēs Etruscōrum nunc singulōs prōvocāre, nunc increpāre omnēs
phrases.english: then, turning fierce and threatening eyes on the Etruscan leaders, he challenged them one by one and taunted them all
in elegy too we challenge the Greeks
